title: Tech Mahindra Posts Third Consecutive Billion-Dollar Quarter in Deal Wins
excerpt: The Pune-based IT services firm reported a 28% jump in net profit and $1.08 billion in new deal wins for Q1 FY27, extending its turnaround streak under CEO Mohit Joshi.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Tech Mahindra's net profit rose 28.4% to ₹1,465 crore ($174 million) in Q1 FY27.
  • New deal total contract value reached $1.08 billion, marking the third consecutive quarter above $1 billion.
  • EBIT margin improved to 14.4%, the 11th straight quarter of margin growth.
  • Brokerages are divided on valuation, with targets ranging from ₹1,270 to ₹1,900.

Q1 FY27 results
  • Net profit rose 28.4% year-on-year to ₹1,465 crore ($174 million) in Q1 FY27, with revenue up 17.7% to ₹15,712 crore.
  • New deal total contract value (TCV) hit $1.08 billion, up 33.3% YoY — the third straight quarter above $1 billion.
  • EBIT margin expanded 60 basis points sequentially to 14.4%, the 11th consecutive quarter of margin improvement.
  • Brokerages are split on valuation: Motilal Oswal targets ₹1,900 (Buy) while Morgan Stanley holds ₹1,270 (Underweight).

A Turnaround Takes Shape

Tech Mahindra delivered its strongest quarterly performance in years, reporting Q1 FY27 results on July 17 that beat analyst expectations across revenue, profit, and deal bookings. The Pune-headquartered IT services firm posted consolidated net profit of ₹1,465 crore, a 28.4% jump from the year-ago quarter, while revenue from operations climbed 17.7% to about ₹15,712 crore.

In dollar terms, revenue reached $1,660 million — up 2.6% quarter-on-quarter in constant currency and 6.6% year-on-year, the fastest growth rate since CEO Mohit Joshi launched the company's three-year transformation programme.

"YoY growth of 6.1% coupled with three consecutive quarters of deal wins exceeding $1 billion underscores the resilience of our business and the growing relevance of our offerings."

- Mohit Joshi, CEO and Managing Director, Tech Mahindra

Deal Pipeline Hits a New Gear

The headline number for investors was deal bookings. New deal TCV came in at $1,078 million, up 33.3% from a year earlier and firmly above the billion-dollar threshold for the third consecutive quarter. The figure builds on a full-year FY26 deal haul of $3.79 billion, itself up 41.6% year-on-year.

Tech Mahindra also expanded its marquee client roster, adding three customers in the $10 million annual revenue bracket and four in the $50 million-plus tier. Joshi pointed to this deepening of client relationships as a sign that the company's repositioned offerings — particularly around AI, cloud, and enterprise transformation — are gaining traction with large global buyers.

Margins Keep Climbing

Operating profitability continued its upward march. EBIT margin expanded 60 basis points sequentially to 14.4%, marking 11 consecutive quarters of improvement. EBITDA climbed 53.5% year-on-year to ₹2,264 crore.

CFO Rohit Anand attributed the margin gains to disciplined working capital management, a leaner employee pyramid, and reduced subcontracting costs. The company's headcount stood at 146,760, down 863 from the previous quarter, while IT attrition held steady at 11.8% on a last-twelve-months basis.

Management reiterated its target of reaching 15% EBIT margin by the end of FY27, though it flagged that wage hikes effective in Q2 and continued AI investments would create near-term headwinds.

Analysts Divided on What Comes Next

The results drew a wide range of reactions from brokerages. Motilal Oswal, the most bullish, reiterated a Buy with a ₹1,900 target, calling Tech Mahindra its preferred large-cap IT pick. Anand Rathi set a ₹1,762 target, citing a projected 23.5% adjusted EPS compound annual growth rate over FY26-28. JM Financial raised its target to ₹1,670 from ₹1,525.

On the cautious side, Morgan Stanley maintained its Underweight rating at ₹1,270, flagging de-rating risk once margins normalise. Jefferies held an Underperform call at ₹1,260, arguing that valuations at roughly 20 times earnings are too rich. Citi maintained a Sell at ₹1,345, noting that part of the Q1 beat was aided by one-time revenue and lower selling, general, and administrative expenses.

Shares traded at ₹1,530.70 on the NSE on July 18 morning, up 1.35% from the previous close.

Manufacturing Boost, but a One-Off

Among verticals, manufacturing led sequential growth at 9% quarter-on-quarter, partly aided by accelerated delivery of a European automotive programme. Management cautioned that this tailwind would not repeat in Q2, tempering expectations for near-term vertical outperformance.

Sandeep Shah, Director of Equity Research at Equirus Securities, said the strong start to the year implied Tech Mahindra would meet its FY27 commitments "without big challenges, unless macro concerns deteriorate further."

What It Means for Indian IT

Tech Mahindra's Q1 results contrast sharply with peer Wipro, which reported declining margins and cautious forward guidance in the same quarter. The divergence highlights how execution on cost discipline and deal conversion can differentiate companies even in a softening global demand environment. For the Indian IT sector — and the tens of thousands of professionals it employs across the US, Europe, and the Middle East — sustained deal momentum at firms like Tech Mahindra signals continued hiring demand in specialised areas such as AI, sovereign cloud, and enterprise platforms.
